Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Voss, CEO; Jane Hargrove, CFO; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Voss.

Elena Voss:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a pivotal quarter for Voltara Motors. We made significant strides in key areas, including record delivery volumes across our model lineup and regions, continued declines in battery costs per kWh that are accelerating our path to profitability, expanded gross margins through mix shifts and cost efficiencies, and ambitious capital expenditure plans to scale manufacturing and secure supply chains. We are particularly excited about the upcoming launch of the VTAR-Semi, our dedicated electric semi-truck platform, and its anticipated expansion of our total addressable market into commercial fleets, targeting a 15% share in the Class 8 segment by 2027.

These achievements position us strongly in the EV transition, where we're leveraging our multi-gigafactory footprint, autonomy stack, and vertical integration to outpace competitors. Now, I'll turn the call over to Jane Hargrove to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jane Hargrove:
Thank you, Elena, and good morning, everyone. For Q3, our revenue reached $18.2 billion, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin expanded to 19.2%, up significantly from prior periods, while operating expenses were controlled at $4.1 billion. Net income came in at $1.2 billion. We are maintaining a strong balance sheet with $12.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our guidance for next quarter points to revenue of $19.5 to $20.5 billion, with continued margin expansion.

Before we open the line for Q&A, let me provide more color on our key operational and financial drivers, starting with our Q3 delivery results, which remain our North Star metric in the EV industry, directly tying into revenue recognition under ASC 606, production throughput from our gigafactories, and our path to sustained positive free cash flow.

In Q3, we delivered a record 285,164 vehicles globally, marking an 18% year-over-year increase from 241,800 in Q3 2023, and a solid 6% quarter-over-quarter sequential uptick from 269,000 in Q2. This exceeded our guidance midpoint of 275,000 units, driven by accelerated production ramps at Giga Texas and Giga Shanghai, improved 4680 cell yields now exceeding 92%—up from 85% a year ago—and targeted inventory destocking in key markets. Model mix shifted toward higher-margin SUVs and trucks, boosting our blended average selling price to $48,200, a 4% QoQ improvement despite competitive pricing pressures.

Our portfolio continues to emphasize scalable platforms built on our next-gen structural battery pack architecture, which integrates LFP cathodes for cost efficiency in entry models and NMC for premium range. By model, the VTAR-3 compact sedan, with an estimated 320-mile EPA range starting at $38,000, delivered 79,500 units, or 28% of total, up 12% YoY. It was a steady performer in fleet and ride-share segments, with an uptick from Q2 due to software update V12.5 enabling unsupervised FSD Beta in 15 markets. The China LFP variant gained 5% share versus BYD Seagull amid subsidy tailwinds, with margins holding at 22% gross.

The VTAR-Y mid-size SUV/crossover, offering 340-mile range starting at $45,000, led with 121,800 deliveries, 43% of total, up 25% YoY. Our Model Y equivalent is now number two globally behind Tesla's Y per EV Volumes data. This record quarter was fueled by Giga Berlin ramping to 5,000 units per week and U.S. IRA-compliant packs qualifying for the full $7,500 credit. Cybertruck ramp cannibalization was minimal at less than 2%.

The VTAR-X full-size luxury SUV, with 405-mile range and Plaid option starting at $85,000, delivered 39,200 units, 14% of total, up 8% YoY. It showed premium resilience despite Lucid and China luxury slowdowns, with 15% YoY ASP growth to $102,000 from HW4 autonomy suite take-rate hitting 68%, up from 52%. Europe demand was soft on 20% tariffs but offset by Saudi exports.

The VTAR-Cyber full-size EV pickup, with 500+ mile range starting at $72,000, exploded to 36,400 deliveries, 12% of total, up 45% YoY. Post-tooling fixes at Giga Texas, we're at a 1,200 per week run-rate. U.S. market share versus F-150 Lightning and Rivian R1T climbed to 18% in pickups over $70,000, driven by towing demos and Ford dealer partnerships for fleet wins.

Finally, the new VTAR-Mini entry compact hatch, 250-mile range starting at $28,000 post-subsidy, delivered 8,264 units, 3% of total since its Q2 launch. Early ramp from Shanghai pilot line showed initial comps 85% YoY to Xiaomi SU7 in China urban markets, scaling to 10,000 per quarter in Q4 with 2170 cell cost-downs.

Model mix trends show SUVs and trucks now at 69% of volume, up from 62% YoY, reflecting consumer shift to family haulers amid high gas prices averaging $3.80 per gallon in the U.S. Entry models including the 3 and Mini at 31% support mass-market penetration, aligning with our 20% cost reduction target via unboxed manufacturing processes akin to Tesla's.

Regionally, we saw balanced growth, with China's 32% share offsetting softer Europe amid subsidy cliffs. North America, covering U.S., Canada, and Mexico, delivered 120,500 units, 42% of total, up 22% YoY. The U.S. alone hit 108,000 units, up 24% YoY. IRA Section 30D credits flowed to 92% of deliveries; Cyber pickup captured 25% of Q3 EV truck sales per Cox Automotive. Texas and Mexico localization at 85% content mitigates tariffs. Q4 guide is plus 10% QoQ on Austin expansion.

China delivered 91,200 units, 32% of total, up 15% YoY. It's a fierce battleground versus BYD's Qin L and Seagull, and Xiaomi. Shanghai Giga hit 8,000 per week; VTAR-Y LFP variant took 8% mid-SUV share per CPCA data. NEV subsidies extended to December 2024 boosted Mini launch. Supply chain edge with in-house cathode production cut costs 12% versus peers. Risk is price wars—ASP down 3% QoQ to 220,000 RMB.

Europe, EU/UK/Nordics, delivered 44,800 units, 16% of total, up 2% YoY. Muted growth post-German EEG subsidy cuts ending in September. Berlin Giga at 75% capacity utilization; VTAR-3 and Y compliant with 95% EU cobalt-free mandate. Versus VW ID.4, we gained 3 percentage points share in Norway and Sweden, now at 22%. EU-China tariff probe upside: our local packs dodge 38% duties.

APAC ex-China, including Australia, Japan, Korea, and India, delivered 19,500 units, 7% of total, up 30% YoY. Hypergrowth in Australia with 12,000 units, up 40% on RAV4 EV waitlists, and India pilot 2,000 via Tata partnership. Japan regulatory hurdles easing for VTAR-Y JDM spec. Focus on right-hand-drive scaling for 5% FY25 mix.

Rest of World, Middle East, LATAM, Africa, delivered 9,164 units, 3% of total, up 50% YoY. Emerging tailwind—Saudi PIF deal delivered 4,000 VTAR-X; Brazil factory MoU for 50,000 per year by 2026. High-thermal packs suit ME climates with 125°F tolerance.

Cross-model and region highlights: North America dominates with 55% of Cyber and 48% of Y—IRA plus truck boom. China skews to 42% of 3 and 35% of Mini for price-sensitive urban buyers. Europe premium with X at 22% regional share, leveraging FSD for Autobahn appeal. Inventory down 15% QoQ to 25,000 units globally, with NA at healthy 10 days' supply.

These deliveries underscore our multi-factory flywheel—three gigas at over 90% utilization, 2170/4680 cell mix optimizing for $0.07 per kWh costs. Technical bets paying off: V13 FSD rollout in Q4 could add 2-3% attach rate premium; structural packs enable 10% range uplift without weight penalty. Headwinds like China's overcapacity—BYD's 3.5 million annualized—prompt agile pricing, like U.S. Y lease at $299 per month capturing Hertz residuals. FY24 full-year guide: 1.15 to 1.2 million deliveries, plus 35% YoY. Q4 at 310,000 midpoint, front-loaded ramps for Semi pilot of 1,000 units.

We're positioned for 20% plus CAGR through 2027, outpacing IHS Markit EV forecasts via localization at 85% NA/China content and autonomy monetization.

Shifting to another critical lever for profitability: battery costs per kWh, the lifeblood of our cost structure, accounting for roughly 35-40% of bill of materials for flagships like the VTAR-Y and Cyber. In Q3—aligning with our Q2 trajectory—we achieved average battery pack cost of $92 per kWh at the pack level, down 17% year-over-year and 22% sequentially. This is for high-volume NMC 811 chemistry packs delivering 250-300 Wh/kg energy density and supporting 800+ km range on long-range variants. For context, this aligns with Tesla's 4680 cell economics and beats most legacy OEMs still at $110-120 per kWh. Our LFP packs for entry-level models came in at $68 per kWh, benefiting from higher cell-to-pack ratios—now 68% versus industry average 55%—thanks to CATL's Shenxing SuperFast Charging cells.

Industry-wide, the trajectory is steeply downward, with BloombergNEF at $139 per kWh global average in 2023, a 14% drop from 2022 and 89% decline since 2015. We're ahead, with cumulative 92% reductions through scale, innovation, and supply chain discipline. Key drivers: economies of scale from Nevada Gigafactory Phase 2 ramp to 100 GWh annual capacity, slashing per-unit depreciation and overhead by 25%. We procure over 80 GWh annually, qualifying for volume rebates from LG Energy Solution and Panasonic.

Chemistry shifts: LFP adoption to 45% of packs, up from 25% YoY, structurally 20-30% lower cost than NMC due to abundant iron-phosphate and no cobalt/nickel. Mirrors BYD's Blade Battery below $60 per kWh at scale.

Manufacturing innovations: dry electrode coating in 15% of lines cut solvent recovery by 40%, yield to 98%. Piloting 46-series cylindricals with tabless design for 20% higher C-rates, 15% savings via reduced interconnects.

Regionally bifurcated: China at $55-65 per kWh for LFP via CATL/BYD dominance, 60% plus global share, enabling aggressive pricing from XPeng/NIO. U.S. at $105 per kWh from Ultium Cells JV with GM, but full $35 per kWh IRA credit nets $70. Europe lags at $120-140 due to tariffs and REACH, but EU Net-Zero Industry Act spurs local builds like Northvolt.

Ahead, guiding $80 per kWh average by end-2025, sub-$60 by 2027 per McKinsey's $58 forecast. Assumes silicon anode for 10-15% density at minimal premium, solid-state pilots in 2026, 75% plus cell-to-module-to-pack. Locked multi-year offtakes: 40 GWh CATL at volume discounts, SK On for 4680-equivalent prismatics.

These trends transform: every $10 per kWh reduction to EBITDA—$1,200+ savings per 100 kWh pack on VTAR-Y, enabling 8% ASP cuts while expanding margins. Fortifies moat versus ICE like Ford/Stellantis as costs hit $100 parity. De-risking via 30% in-house cells by 2026, Redwood recycling at 95% recovery, AI supply chain for 5-7% savings.

Battery costs are our rocket fuel—declining faster than consensus, positioning for 20% plus share in $40-60k segment. We're engineering the trend.

On gross margins and outlook, we delivered non-GAAP 19.2% in Q3, up 320 basis points sequentially from Q2. Strongest since scaling Apex 400 platform equivalent, driven by mix to high-margin VTAR-X SUV at 45% deliveries, and COGS reductions from in-house 4680 ramp.

Raising FY2024 gross margin guidance to 22-24%, from 20-22%. Q4 at 21-23%, reflecting cost-downs amid softer volumes. Embeds conservative $100 million headwind from IRA passthroughs to fleets, offset by $150 million Shanghai Giga 2.0 efficiencies.

Key assumptions by drivers: product mix/pricing for 200 bps expansion—55-60% premium models by year-end versus 40% Q3, VTAR-X and new Cyber Max truck at $72k MSRP. ASP up 4-6% QoQ to $58k FY, selective increases like $2,500 on VTAR-3 in NA, reduced discounting at 45 days inventory. 2% FX tailwind weaker USD vs RMB, 25% export revenue.

Manufacturing scale/fixed leverage for 150 bps: 280-300k FY deliveries, 25% up, Q4 85k as Fremont East at 95% utilization on structural packs. Breakeven drops to 1,200/week per plant. Cell-to-module-to-pack full by Q4 cuts battery BOM 18% versus cylindrical NMC. $450 per vehicle savings Q3, proprietary silicon-anode for 15% density at lower cobalt.

Supply chain/commodities for 300 bps: cells to $78-82/kWh year-end from $92, CATL/LGES oversupply, BYD LFP at 40/60 blend. Lithium $12k/tonne down 60% YoY, nickel $16.5k. Semis stable, TSMC ASICs 12% power electronics savings. 70% in-sourced batteries/motors save $800/EV, gigacasting on Cyber Max cuts body-in-white 25%, Giga Press style.

Regionally: North America 65% revenue, IRA $7,500 at 70% capture, U.S. content 60% to 75% 2025. Rivian/Ford pressure, but 350 kW charging loyalty. Europe 20%, BYD tariffs 10% premium, Berlin 50k H2 run-rate, subsidy phase-out weighs. China/APAC 15%, Shanghai 28% margins vs global 19%, 5% compression price wars—VTAR-3 undercuts Model 3 8% at 189k RMB, SEA exports offset.

This positions for 1,000 bps+ to mid-30s by 2026, outpacing Lucid negatives, matching GM 23%. Enablers: $2.5B 2024 capex U.S. cathodes/Redwood JV, Apex OS subs 75% gross. Risks: lithium volatility +/-10%, U.S. Mexico tariffs 80% mitigated, macro 10% volume delay. 18-month backlog, 40% R&D de-risks. Gross margins North Star for H1 2025 FCF positive.

Finally, our capital expenditure plans and investment priorities for FY2024 and beyond. We're entering a pivotal EV transition phase where scale, vertical integration, and tech leadership separate winners—like Tesla's gigafactory playbook or BYD's LFP dominance.

FY2024 capex guided $12.8 billion, 22% up from $10.5 billion FY2023, to double capacity to 2 million units annually by 2026. Funded 60% operating cash flow $9.1 billion YTD, 25% $4 billion green bond, 15% equipment leases. Net debt/EBITDA 1.2x, below Rivian 3.5x, firepower amid Europe demand softness.

Capex laser-focused: manufacturing scale-up 42% at $5.4 billion; next-gen R&D 28% $3.6 billion; supply chain resilience 25% $3.2 billion; balance digital/corporate.

Manufacturing first: gigafactory expansions for IRA incentives, localization. North America $2.1 billion Savannah, Georgia—like Hyundai Metaplant—ramping 500k/year Q4 2025, full $7,500 PTC. Includes $800 million 4680 line, 20% costs down vs 2170 via 280 Wh/kg, dry electrode. Europe $1.2 billion Berlin-Brandenburg for EU 16% recycled by 2031, Enyaq SUV +40%. APAC $1.1 billion CATL JV Thailand LFP, hedging China 100% tariffs, ASEAN EV pen 15% 2023 from 5% 2021.

R&D $3.6 billion up 35% YoY, 65% powertrain/autonomy. Batteries $1.2 billion solid-state Troy, Michigan for 400 Wh/kg, 1,000+ cycles 2027—vs QuantumScape. Silicon-anode 15% range boost Atlas sedan. Autonomy $900 million Level 4 DriveOS with Luminar LiDAR, NVIDIA Orin-X, ahead GM Super Cruise robotaxi. Software $600 million OTA 12% efficiency gains fleet-wide like Tesla FSD.

Supply chain $3.2 billion: $1.5 billion U.S./Australia cathode precursors, 80% NMC domestic 2026, less Congo cobalt up 25% YTD. $700 million TSMC semis fabs, lead times 52 to 20 weeks. Recycling $400 million Redwood black mass, 95% recovery, 10-15% BOM savings.

Regionally: NA 45% $5.8B IRA tailwinds, U.S. content 65% $1.2B credits. Europe 30% $3.8B CO2 95g/km 2025, 12% EV contraction Germany subsidies. China/APAC 20% $2.6B LFP mass-market vs BYD Qin. India 5% $500M Pune 48V hybrids, 30% YoY surge.

This mix de-risks 25% EBITDA margins 2026 from 12% today, 15-20% COGS deflation. Ahead Ford Model e $1.3B Q3 losses, premium SUVs 55% mix $65k ASP. Risks semis volatility, lithium +18% MoM, but 70% Albemarle fixed.

This $12.8B is owning EV stack mine-to-mileage. 85% FY2024 PO'd, executing flawlessly.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Mike Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Analyst 1:
Thanks, good morning. Great delivery beat this quarter. Can you elaborate on the China pricing dynamics and how you're protecting margins there amid the price wars?

Elena Voss:
Thanks, Mike. China remains intensely competitive, as we highlighted, with BYD and others pushing volumes. Our Shanghai Giga's in-house cathode production gives us a 12% cost edge, allowing VTAR-Y LFP to capture 8% mid-SUV share without deep cuts. ASP dipped 3% QoQ but stabilized via NEV subsidies to December. We're agile—targeted leases and FSD betas add premium—and FY guide holds 1.15-1.2M total, so no major revisions.

Operator:
Our next question from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Hi team, on battery costs—impressive $92/kWh. With LFP ramp, what's the risk to NMC pricing from China oversupply, and update on solid-state timeline?

Jane Hargrove:
Hi Sarah. China oversupply is a tailwind actually, locking CATL at escalating discounts for 40 GWh. Blended NMC/LFP 55/45 keeps us at $80/kWh 2025 guide. Solid-state prototypes Troy skunkworks on track for 400 Wh/kg pilots 2026, 1,000-cycle life de-risked via silicon anode bridge. Regional nets like IRA $70 effective U.S. solidify this.

Operator:
Next from David Kim with JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:
Congrats on capex discipline. With $12.8B, how does Savannah IRA qualification progress, and Europe recycling compliance?

Elena Voss:
Thanks David. Savannah mirrors Hyundai's setup—$2.1B ramps 500k/year Q4 2025, 4680 line $800M for full $7,500 PTC, 65% U.S. content unlocking $1.2B credits FY. Europe Berlin $1.2B hits EU 16% recycled 2031, Enyaq +40% output. Net debt 1.2x keeps flexibility versus peers.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:
Our final question from Lisa Chen with Barclays.

Analyst 4:
Solid margin raise to 22-24%. Key swing factor for Q4, and capex ROI assumptions?

Jane Hargrove:
Lisa, thanks. Q4 21-23% hinges scale—Q4 85k deliveries Fremont 95% util, cell-to-pack 18% BOM cut. Mix 55-60% premium, ASP $58k, $78-82/kWh cells. Upside supply chain lithium down 60% YoY. Capex ROI targets 25% EBITDA 2026 via 15-20% COGS deflation, vertical 30% cells. FCF H1 2025 locked.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Voss for closing remarks.

Elena Voss:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident that Voltara Motors is well-positioned for continued success in the rapidly evolving automotive landscape. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.

Delivery volume by model and geographic region
Battery costs per kWh and trends
Gross margin guidance and key assumptions

aspect_summary.Capital expenditure plans and investment: FY2024 capex $12.8B (up 22% YoY), focused on doubling capacity to 2M units annually by 2026: 42% ($5.4B) manufacturing expansions (NA $2.1B Savannah GA for 500k/year ramp Q4 2025 with 4680 line, Europe $1.2B Berlin, APAC $1.1B CATL Thailand JV); 28% ($3.6B) R&D (batteries $1.2B solid-state, autonomy $900M); 25% ($3.2B) supply chain (cathodes, semis, Redwood recycling). Funded 60% OCF, 25% green bonds.
aspect_summary.Delivery volume by model and geographic: Q3 record 285,164 vehicles (up 18% YoY): VTAR-3 79,500 (28%), VTAR-Y 121,800 (43%), VTAR-X 39,200 (14%), VTAR-Cyber 36,400 (12%), VTAR-Mini 8,264 (3%). Regions: North America 120,500 (42%, US 108k), China 91,200 (32%), Europe 44,800 (16%), APAC ex-China 19,500 (7%), Rest of World 9,164 (3%). FY24 guide 1.15-1.2M, Q4 310k midpoint.
aspect_summary.Battery costs per kWh and trends: Q3 pack avg $92/kWh (down 17% YoY, 22% QoQ) for NMC 811; LFP $68/kWh. Drivers: scale (Nevada 100 GWh), LFP 45% mix, dry electrode/yields. Regional: China $55-65 LFP, US $105 net $70 w/IRA, Europe $120-140. Guide: $80/kWh end-2025, sub-$60 by 2027 via silicon anode/solid-state.
aspect_summary.Gross margin guidance and key assumption: Q3 non-GAAP 19.2% (up 320 bps QoQ). FY2024 raised to 22-24%, Q4 21-23%. Key assumptions: mix/pricing (200 bps, 55-60% premium, ASP $58k), manufacturing scale (150 bps, cell-to-pack cuts), supply chain (300 bps, cells $78-82/kWh, lithium down 60% YoY); embeds IRA headwinds offset by efficiencies.
